title: Well-Nested Tags
statement: A markup document has been split into tokens. An opening tag looks like `<name>`, a closing tag looks like `</name>`, and a self-closing tag looks like `<name/>`. Every other token is plain text.

The document is *well nested* if every opening tag is closed by a matching closing tag, and tags close in the reverse order they were opened. Self-closing tags and text never need closing. Return whether `tokens` is well nested.
constraints: tag names are 1 to 10 lowercase letters
hints: What do you need to remember about the tags that are open right now, and which one has to close next?
Push the name of each opening tag on a stack. A closing tag has to match the name on top.
At the end the stack has to be empty, and a closing tag that arrives when the stack is empty fails right away.
pitfalls: Not checking that the stack is empty at the end.
Popping from an empty stack on a stray closing tag.
Treating self-closing tags as opening tags.

Comparing raw tokens instead of tag names, so

interviewerNotes: Ask how they tell the four kinds of token apart.
